THE PROBLEM, measured on real media. A two-person podcast composite mixes two grid-aligned speaker stems with plain amix. Measurements on the same 12s span of the host speaking:
- host stem alone: spectral centroid 2200Hz (crisp), speech RMS -23.9dB
- guest CHANNEL during host speech: RMS -22.8dB (LOUDER than the host!) and dull (1257Hz) -- it is bleed/echo of the host's voice re-recorded through the guest's end, not silence
- the amix result: 1604Hz -- muffled, because the crisp direct voice is summed with a loud dull delayed copy
- amix(host,host) control: 2202Hz -- amix itself is transparent; the guest channel's bleed is the cause
- separately, the guest's own speech is ~15dB quieter than the host's (RMS -38.9 vs -23.9): a large speaker imbalance.
A noise gate cannot fix the bleed (it is at -22.8dB, far above any noise threshold, and speech-correlated).

THE FIX: make the stems-mode composite a SPEAKER-AWARE AUTO-MIX inside av_sync.py:
1. DUCKING BY SPEAKER TIMELINE. The repo already computes per-frame speaker states from the isolated stems: audio_energy.aligned_envelopes(host,guest,offsets,hop) then angle_editor.classify_frames(host_db,guest_db) yielding 'host'/'guest'/'two'/'sil' per frame (this drives the camera). Reuse EXACTLY that (import audio_energy and angle_editor; do not reimplement classification). Build per-stem volume automation: during 'host' frames the guest input is attenuated by DUCK_DB (named constant, -60dB is right: kills bleed while any genuine louder interjection reclassifies as 'two' or its own turn), and vice versa; during 'two' both stay open at 0dB; during 'sil' hold the previous state. Smooth every transition with a ramp (~60ms) so ducking never clicks. Implement the automation as a generated ffmpeg volume expression or per-segment volume+concat inside the stems-mode composite filter graph -- your choice, but it must be deterministic and land in the SAME filter graph build_composite_filter (or its stems-mode variant) already produces, preserving the existing -copyts/aresample timing semantics EXACTLY. Timing must not shift by a sample: only per-input gain changes.
2. SPEAKER LOUDNESS MATCH. Before the duck/mix, apply a per-stem static gain that brings each speaker's DOMINANT-speech level to a common target: measure each stem's mean RMS over ITS OWN dominant frames (from the same classification), compute gain = SPEECH_TARGET_DB (named constant, -20dB) minus that measurement, clamp to +/-MAX_SPEAKER_GAIN_DB (named constant, 14dB) so a broken measurement cannot blast a channel. The ~15dB-quiet guest gets lifted to parity; the host stays roughly unchanged.
3. Keep raw-tracks (non-stems) mode byte-identical to today; this applies ONLY to the stems-mode path. Expose the new behaviour as the default for stems mode with an escape hatch kwarg (auto_mix=True default) so a plain sum remains testable.

TESTS (tests/test_composite_ducking.py, pure/mocked, no real ffmpeg): (1) generated automation ducks the guest during host frames and vice versa, with 'two' leaving both open (feed a synthetic state sequence); (2) transition ramps exist (no instantaneous gain step) -- assert the expression/segments encode the ramp duration; (3) speaker gains: a guest measured 15dB under target gets ~+15dB (within clamp) and gains are clamped at MAX_SPEAKER_GAIN_DB (negative test: a 40dB-quiet measurement must NOT produce +40dB); (4) raw-tracks mode filter output is UNCHANGED vs the previous implementation (negative test: assert no duck/volume automation appears in raw mode); (5) auto_mix=False yields the old plain stems mix. Mock audio_energy/classify_frames with synthetic envelopes.
